There are 2 main factors:

  1. Shot placement.

  2. Hydrostatic shock.

Shot placement is about knowledge and proficiency. You have to know where to shoot, and be disciplined and experienced enough to be able to do so under pressure. Practice and education are key.

Hydrostatic shock has to do with velocity and bullet type. Usually the faster the bullet, the better the hydrostatic shock - however this can mean the bullet will pass through the target before being able to impart most of its energy. This is where self-defence hollowpoint rounds come into play. A hollow point will mushroom and splinter upon impact with an un-armored target, thus imparting most of its energy in a giant shockwave inside the target before exiting. If you shoot a solid round, this can still kill the target, but may not stop it instantly due to the lack of shock.

Know your equipment, educate yourself, and practice often.
